advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface the new invalid-key ValueError cleanly at the bridge projects set/remove callers (catch ValueError alongside RebarError, or raise RebarError) so operator key typos yield a clean error message and controlled exit rather than a traceback.
evidence: _lib_ops.py:132-137 catches only `except KeyError as exc:` around `store.remove_project(...)`, mapping KeyError->RebarError; a ValueError from _require_valid_key is not caught
_cli/_bridge_commands.py:363-373: the 'set' verb calls `rebar.bridge_projects_set(...)` with no try/except, and 'remove' has `except RebarError as exc:` only — neither catches ValueError
_cli/__init__.py:499-510: the top-level main() boundary catches only RemovedInputError and TrackerRootError, so a propagating ValueError becomes an uncaught traceback
advisory.finding: The newly-introduced ValueError for a syntactically-invalid project key is not caught by any of the existing clean-error boundaries on the set/remove CLI paths, so an operator typo surfaces as a raw Python traceback instead of a clean 'Error: ...' message with a controlled exit code.
scenarios: `rebar bridge projects set le-g rebar` (or `remove le-g`) from the CLI with a malformed key
MCP bridge_projects_set/remove invoked with a malformed key

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that remove_project(tmp_path, <valid existing key>) succeeds: the key is deleted from projects.json and load_mapping no longer contains it.
evidence: The diff inserts `_require_valid_key(key)` as the first statement of remove_project (projects_store.py:185), gating the entire remove path.
Only remove_project test added is test_remove_project_rejects_invalid_key_before_mutation (line 144), which asserts the INVALID path only (`pytest.raises(ValueError)` + file unchanged).
test_set_project_accepts_valid_key_and_writes (line 134) covers the valid WRITE path for set_project, but there is no analogous valid-remove test.

search_files for 'remove_project' across tests/unit/rebar_reconciler returns only the two lines in this file (invalid-key test + comment); happy-path file test_projects_store_happy.py has no remove_project reference — ABSENCE of any valid-remove coverage.
advisory.finding: No test covers remove_project's valid-key happy path after the new `_require_valid_key` guard was inserted: there is no assertion that a syntactically-valid key still removes an existing project (guard passes, record mutated and re-persisted). A regression where the new guard wrongly rejects valid keys, or otherwise breaks the valid-remove path, would go undetected.
scenarios: A future edit tightens `_require_valid_key` (or reorders the guard) so it rejects an otherwise-valid key; remove_project silently stops working for real keys and no test fails.
The guard is accidentally placed after the KeyError check or the del, changing observable ordering, with no valid-path test to catch it.
